description: Comprehensive iOS app production readiness initiative based on a deep security, UX, and infrastructure audit. Covers wildcard CORS migration across all edge functions, Apple Sign-In implementation, pagination, offline support, input validation, accessibility, dark mode, realtime subscriptions, and crash reporting. Priority 1 items are App Store blockers or critical security. Priority 2 are high-impact UX/security. Priority 3 are polish and completeness.

userStories.title: Migrate remaining edge functions from wildcard CORS to secure-cors.ts
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want all Supabase edge functions to use whitelist-based CORS from _shared/secure-cors.ts instead of wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. Currently ~165 remaining edge functions import from _shared/cors.ts or define inline wildcard CORS headers. For each function: (1) replace `import { corsHeaders } from '../_shared/cors.ts'` with `import { getCorsHeaders, handleCorsPreflightRequest } from '../_shared/secure-cors.ts'`, (2) replace the static `corsHeaders` usage with `const corsHeaders = getCorsHeaders(req)` at the top of the handler, (3) replace OPTIONS handling with `return handleCorsPreflightRequest(req)`. Work in batches of 20-30 functions per iteration. Start with security-critical functions: api-auth, dos-protection, reset-password-otp, send-auth-otp, verify-auth-otp.
acceptanceCriteria: api-auth/index.ts uses getCorsHeaders(req) instead of wildcard CORS
dos-protection/index.ts uses getCorsHeaders(req) instead of wildcard CORS
reset-password-otp/index.ts uses getCorsHeaders(req) instead of wildcard CORS
send-auth-otp/index.ts uses getCorsHeaders(req) instead of wildcard CORS
verify-auth-otp/index.ts uses getCorsHeaders(req) instead of wildcard CORS
No edge function in this batch contains Access-Control-Allow-Origin: '*'
npm run build passes
npm run lint passes
userStories.notes: COMPLETE (2026-08-19). api-auth was the only one of the five still on inline wildcard CORS; dos-protection, reset-password-otp, send-auth-otp and verify-auth-otp were already on secure-cors from earlier work. api-auth now imports getCorsHeaders/handleCorsPreflightRequest, derives corsHeaders per request inside the serve handler, and returns handleCorsPreflightRequest(req) for OPTIONS. scripts/check-edge-function-auth.mjs reports 0 wildcard-CORS violations.

userStories.notes: IN PROGRESS (2026-08-19). Repo-wide sweep took wildcard-CORS functions from 94 to 30. 103 functions were migrated by a checked script (drop the module-level wildcard corsHeaders literal, import from _shared/secure-cors.ts, derive `const corsHeaders = getCorsHeaders(req)` as the first statement of the handler, and route OPTIONS through handleCorsPreflightRequest(req)). The script refused any file where corsHeaders was referenced outside the handler body, where the handler param was unnamed, or where a second corsHeaders declaration existed. Hand-migrated on top: api-auth, projects and time-tracking (inline literal nested in the OPTIONS branch), create-missing-content (the last importer of the deprecated _shared/cors.ts). _shared/cors.ts is now a shim re-exporting secure-cors rather than hardcoding '*'. Verified: all 108 changed files parse clean under the TypeScript parser; corsHeaders is declared before first use in every file and the getCorsHeaders() argument matches the handler's own request param; check-edge-function-auth.mjs reports 0 wildcard violations. REMAINING 30 functions need real per-file work, not a script: each threads corsHeaders into module-level helper functions, so the helpers need a corsHeaders parameter (or the handler needs to close over them). userStories.title: Fix realtime subscription memory leak in JobCostListViewModel
userStories.description: As a developer, I want realtime subscriptions properly cleaned up so the app doesn't leak memory.
